title: At the WKU cafeteria
paragraphs: My name is Nurgul Abenova. I am 18 years old and I am from Taraz. I study Biology at WKU in Uralsk. One of the best things about living in the dormitory is the university cafeteria. It is on the ground floor of the main academic building, and it is open every day from 7:00 am to 8:00 pm. More than 500 students eat there every day. For me, the cafeteria is not just a place to eat — it is a place to relax, talk, and feel like part of the WKU community.

The cafeteria serves breakfast from 7:00 to 9:30 every morning. There is always some porridge — usually oat or millet — and some fresh bread with butter. There are also eggs: fried, boiled, or scrambled. I always have some hot tea with my breakfast — either black Kazakh tea with milk or sweet green tea. There is also some orange juice and some apple juice available. On special days, there are fresh baursaks on the breakfast table. I never skip breakfast — my mother always says that breakfast gives you energy for the whole day!

Lunch is my favourite meal of the day. The lunch menu changes every day, but there are always some traditional options. There is always some soup — borscht, chicken noodle soup, or the delicious shurpa with lamb. After the soup, there is a main course: usually some rice or some mashed potatoes with meat or fish. There are also some fresh salads with vegetables. And there is always some compote — the sweet traditional fruit drink that I love. A full lunch costs only 600 tenge, which is very affordable for a student.

On Fridays, the cafeteria serves something very special: beshbarmak! Beshbarmak is the most famous traditional Kazakh dish — large flat noodles with tender boiled meat and rich broth. There is always a long queue on Fridays because every student wants some beshbarmak. They also sometimes serve manty — steamed dumplings filled with meat and onion — and kurt, the small salty dried cheese balls that are a classic Kazakh snack. These dishes always remind me of home and my grandmother's cooking.

The cafeteria also offers some international food options. There is sometimes some pasta with tomato sauce, some fried rice with vegetables, and some pizza on Thursdays. My friend Ruslan loves the pasta because he prefers vegetarian food. He doesn't eat much meat, so he always looks for some vegetables, some eggs, or some cheese options on the menu. The cafeteria tries to have something for everyone — meat lovers, vegetarians, and students who just want something simple and fast.

There are many drinks available in the cafeteria. You can always find some black tea, some green tea, some compote, and some mineral water. There is also some fresh juice — usually apple or orange. On cold winter mornings, there is some hot chocolate too, which is very popular with students. If you want some coffee, there is a small coffee machine near the entrance — you can get some espresso or some cappuccino for 200 tenge. I usually drink two glasses of water with every meal because my Biology teacher says hydration is essential for concentration.

My classmate Ruslan Dzhaksybekov is from Semey and he studies Engineering. He eats in the cafeteria every day too. He always has some soup and some salad for lunch — he never orders any fried food. He says that good food helps him think better during long Engineering lectures. He brings some fruit from the market every Sunday — some apples, some bananas, or some grapes — and keeps them in his room as healthy snacks. He never buys any chips or any sweet biscuits from the student shop.

I believe that eating well is one of the most important habits for a successful student. When I eat some nutritious food for breakfast, I can concentrate better in my Biology lectures. When I drink some water regularly, I feel more energetic and alert. The WKU cafeteria makes healthy eating easy and affordable. My advice to all new students: eat breakfast every morning, drink some water with every meal, and try the beshbarmak on Fridays — you will not be disappointed!

dialogue.speaker: Ruslan
dialogue.text: Nurgul! Over here — I saved you a seat. What are you having today?

dialogue.speaker: Nurgul
dialogue.text: I want some beshbarmak! It's Friday — finally! Are there any left?

dialogue.speaker: Ruslan
dialogue.text: Yes, there is some left but the queue is long. I got some pasta instead.

dialogue.speaker: Nurgul
dialogue.text: Pasta again? Don't you want any meat today?

dialogue.speaker: Ruslan
dialogue.text: No, I don't want any meat. I prefer some vegetables and some cheese.

dialogue.speaker: Nurgul
dialogue.text: Fair enough! Is there any soup left today? I always start with some soup.

dialogue.speaker: Ruslan
dialogue.text: Yes! There is some shurpa — it smells amazing. And there is some fresh bread.

dialogue.speaker: Nurgul
dialogue.text: Perfect. Do you have any compote? I can't find any on this table.

dialogue.speaker: Ruslan
dialogue.text: Here — I got some for you. I also have some mineral water if you want.

dialogue.speaker: Nurgul
dialogue.text: Thank you! Oh — do they have any baursaks today? I saw some near the door.

dialogue.speaker: Ruslan
dialogue.text: I didn't see any baursaks. But there are some apples near the cashier.

dialogue.speaker: Nurgul
dialogue.text: I'll get some after lunch! I love Fridays at the WKU cafeteria!
